The converse requires positivity and physical normalization without incorrectly identifying all positive matrices with experiments or assuming adaptive testers can be physically twirled.

The Gaussian moment normalization and Schur-block multiplicity factors are consistent. The direct Kostka/Muirhead argument establishes the required balanced minimum without depending on an uninspected general Schur inequality. Pointwise optimality justifies the compact-family result without an unsupported minimax interchange.

Theorem 4.1 supplies both sides of the exponent estimate, including nonzero query remainders. The homogeneous-polynomial evaluation bound and Maclaurin inequality support the lower bound, while trace preservation supplies contraction and the upper bound. The continuity argument also handles changing Choi rank.

Theorem 5.1 derives an exact, strategy-independent threshold from nonvanishing minors, rather than merely exhibiting a successful antisymmetric test. The alpha<1 condition and the absence of a bypass reference at the threshold are correctly specified.

The tensor-stability argument correctly distinguishes ordinary matrix-space rank from noncommutative rank. Its elementary shrunk-subspace bound applies to every partner, and the converse uses the depolarizing channel's full matrix Kraus span. The enlarged global-unitary null is repeatedly made explicit.

The qubit formulas have consistent Choi and spin-flip normalizations. Both tensor examples optimize over complex coefficient spaces, not merely real witnesses; the congruence reduction and signed-minor bound support the stated sharp constants.

summary: Version v1 presents a coherent analytic solution of the stated rotation-invariant minimax problem. The positive-tester reduction, Gaussian–Schur identity and balanced-partition inequality support the universal optimizer; polynomial sphere bounds then yield the determinant exponent and sharp perfect-query threshold. Tensor stability is a properly delimited application of classical noncommutative rank, and the two Werner–Holevo constants appear correctly derived and normalized. I found no unresolved objection capable of invalidating a main theorem. Minor revision is appropriate for abstract wording, RNG metadata and auditability improvements. This assessment is based on static inspection of the supplied parsed PDF and source text: I did not render or independently hash the PDF, execute programs, browse sources or certify worldwide priority.
weaknesses: Equation (24) is the least transparent self-contained algebraic step: the manuscript asserts a twelve-variable determinant expansion and provides supporting scripts. A short Schur-complement or polarized-determinant derivation would make the exact six-dimensional maximum easier to audit without symbolic execution.

The universal result is specific to a strong nuisance-symmetry model and unrestricted reference size. Exponentially growing multiplicity references and difficult determinant optimization limit immediate implementation value. These limitations are acknowledged, but should remain prominent when describing broader applications.

The supplied environment.json does not record CVXPY/Clarabel versions used by standalone schur_checks.py, and review/verify_independent.py inserts an author-specific Windows package path. A portable full-suite dependency specification would improve executable reproducibility; these issues do not affect the analytic proofs.

The proposed novelty is plausible and carefully delimited, but comparisons with the closest cited quantum-testing and matrix-space works were not independently verified here.
